# 1 Kings Chapter 17 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Now Elijah, from Tishbe in Gilead, confronted Ahab: "As the LORD, the God of Israel, lives — the God I serve — there will be no dew or rain in the coming years unless I say so."

**2** Then the LORD told Elijah,

**3** "Leave here. Go east and hide by the brook Cherith, east of the Jordan.

**4** You will drink from the brook, and I have ordered ravens to feed you there."

**5** Elijah did what the LORD said. He went and stayed by the brook Cherith, east of the Jordan.

**6** Ravens brought him bread and meat every morning and evening, and he drank from the brook.

**7** But after a while the brook dried up, because there had been no rain.

**8** Then the LORD said to him,

**9** "Get up and go to Zarephath in Sidon and stay there. I have directed a widow there to provide for you."

**10** So he went to Zarephath. When he arrived at the town gate, a widow was there gathering sticks. He called out to her, "Would you please bring me a little water in a cup so I can have a drink?"

**11** As she was going to get it, he called after her, "And please bring me a piece of bread too."

**12** She replied, "As surely as the LORD your God lives, I don't have a single piece of bread. All I have is a handful of flour in a jar and a little olive oil in a jug. I was just gathering a few sticks to make one last meal for my son and myself. After that, we'll starve."

**13** Elijah said to her, "Don't be afraid. Go home and do as you planned. But first, make a small loaf for me and bring it out. Then make something for yourself and your son.

**14** For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'The flour jar will not run out and the oil jug will not run dry until the day the LORD sends rain on the land.'"

**15** She went and did what Elijah told her. And there was food every day for Elijah, the woman, and her family.

**16** The flour jar never ran out and the oil jug never ran dry, just as the LORD had promised through Elijah.

**17** Some time later, the woman's son became ill. He grew worse and worse until he stopped breathing.

**18** The woman said to Elijah, "What do you have against me, man of God? Did you come here to remind God of my sins and kill my son?"

**19** "Give me your son," Elijah said. He took the boy from her arms, carried him upstairs to the room where he was staying, and laid him on his bed.

**20** Then he cried out to the LORD, "LORD my God, are you bringing tragedy even on this widow I'm staying with, by letting her son die?"

**21** He stretched himself over the boy three times and cried out to the LORD, "LORD my God, please let this boy's life return to him!"

**22** The LORD heard Elijah's prayer. The boy's life returned, and he lived.

**23** Elijah picked up the boy, carried him downstairs, and gave him to his mother. "Look," he said. "Your son is alive."

**24** The woman said to Elijah, "Now I know for certain that you are a man of God and that the LORD truly speaks through you."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **17:1 — the prophet from nowhere**: Elijah appears with no introduction, no call story, no credentials — just a confrontation. He walks into the story and shuts down the sky. No prophet in the Bible has a more dramatic entrance.

2. **17:4-6 — ravens**: God feeds his prophet through unclean birds. This is not accidental. The God who controls the rain also controls creatures the purity system declares off-limits. When survival is the issue, God doesn't consult the rule book.

3. **17:9 — to Jezebel's homeland**: The supreme irony of 1 Kings: Elijah, fleeing from Jezebel's influence in Israel, is sent by God to Sidon — Jezebel's own country — where a foreign widow shows more faith than all of Israel. God's provision comes from the last place anyone would look.

4. **17:12 — "and die"**: The widow's matter-of-fact acceptance of death is devastating. She has calculated her remaining resources with the precision of someone who knows exactly how this ends. She is gathering sticks for the last fire.

5. **17:22 — the first resurrection**: The first time in the Bible that a dead person is brought back to life. Elijah's prayer is raw and desperate, his method physical and intimate. The return of the child's breath reverses the drought in microcosm — God restores what death has taken.

— PNEUMA
